text: Visit 1 (Screening) occurs on Day -7 to Day 0. This includes consent and baseline exams.
Visit 2 (Baseline) occurs on Day 0 and includes study drug administration.
Visit 3 occurs on Day 7 for safety labs and symptom review.
Visit 4 occurs on Day 14 for follow-up and questionnaire review.
Visit 5 occurs on Day 28 and includes imaging and physician evaluation.
Participants must follow all study procedures exactly as explained by the study staff.
You must not take non-approved medications without notifying the study doctor.
Alcohol consumption should be limited to one drink per day during the study.
You must avoid starting new supplements during the study period.
Smoking and recreational drug use are not allowed during participation.
Common side effects include nausea, fatigue, headache, dizziness, and dry mouth.
Moderate side effects may include muscle pain, insomnia, or appetite changes.
Serious side effects include fainting, chest pain, or severe allergic reactions.
You should report any new or worsening symptoms immediately.
Side effects can be reported by phone, email, or during your next visit.
The study coordinator is available Monday to Friday, 9am to 5pm.
Missed visits must be rescheduled within 3 business days.
Transportation support may be available upon request.
You must notify the study team if you plan to travel during the study.
Study-related forms must be completed at each visit.
Only acetaminophen is allowed for pain unless otherwise approved.
You must not take ibuprofen, aspirin, naproxen, or other NSAIDs.
Prescription changes must be reviewed by the study doctor.
Herbal supplements are not allowed unless approved.
Bring all medications to each visit for review.
Arrive 15 minutes early for all appointments.
Bring your study ID card to every visit.
Blood samples will be collected at certain visits.
Some visits may take up to 2 hours.
Wear comfortable clothing to your appointments.
Call emergency services if you experience chest pain or difficulty breathing.
Go to the nearest emergency room for fainting or severe bleeding.
Contact the study doctor immediately for serious symptoms.
Do not wait for your next visit if symptoms are severe.
Your safety is the top priority of the study team.
